title: routine.record.v1: a routine record a person wrote
description: The authority a plugin holding 'schedule' asks a run from (host.v1.json x-run-request, record kind 'routine.v1'): WHAT may be started (tenant, engine, prompt) and which plugin may ask for it. WHEN it runs is the plugin's and is not kept here. The core owns the store; only the person writes, changes or removes a record, through the core's own commands, as the owner on the owner-only socket or a paired device (written_by). A plugin's write is refused 'writer_not_allowed' and nothing is stored. record_id, plugin, tenant, engine, prompt, lease_seconds and budget are the person's; kind, prompt_sha256, revision, written_by, written_at, admitted_at, lease, used and last_refusal are the core's. A run asked from the record runs what the record says (tenant, engine, prompt), never what the plugin sends: a plugin that sends another value is refused 'routine_differs', and a record whose prompt no longer matches prompt_sha256 is refused 'routine_changed'; neither is charged. A run asked from the record is refused once its lease has ended or its budget is spent, and the refusal is kept in last_refusal, where the person reads it. Only the person's new admission (a write of the whole record) gives it a longer lease or a larger budget; a change may only shorten or lower them. Every field not listed here is refused.

record_id.description: The id a run.request names (host.v1.json x-run-request record_id).

plugin.description: The one plugin that may ask for a run from this record.

prompt_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the prompt's UTF-8 bytes, as lowercase hex, written by the core at the admission and at every change of the prompt by the person. A start compares the prompt against it, so a prompt changed in the store by anything but the person's commands is refused 'routine_changed'.

lease_seconds.description: How long the lease the person gave lasts, in seconds from the admission. null only where the person's settings say that a record written with no lease has none.

admitted_at.description: When the person last admitted the record whole: its lease and its budget start then.

lease.description: The lease as the core measures it, or null when the record has none.

used.description: How many runs were started from the record since its admission.

last_refusal.description: The last run asked from the record that the core refused, or null.

writer.description: Who wrote the record last: a principal that stands for the person. The server derives it from the way the request came in; it is never read from the request.

budget.description: How many runs the record may start in one admission.

lease.description: clock is how the lease is measured: 'counted' (seconds of the machine's monotonic clock summed across restarts within one boot) or 'wall' (the wall clock, never read as earlier than the latest wall time seen). start and ends are seconds on that clock.

refusal.description: A run asked from the record and refused: why and when; the plugin and the occurrence it was asked with, each only when it was a value in its form (else the field is absent); and, for 'routine_differs', which of tenant, engine and prompt the plugin sent with another value (never the prompt's text). A request that names no record of this store, or a record kind other than 'routine.v1', is not kept here.

occurrence.description: As run.request takes it (host.v1.json x-run-request occurrence): a UTC instant to the second.
